metadata.notice: Camera waypoints for the guided tour. Purely presentational - edit freely.

waypoints.title: Bulacan lowlands overview
waypoints.caption: The province drains from the Sierra Madre in the east to Manila Bay in the west. Everything in this tour sits in that gradient.

waypoints.title: Angat River and the upper catchment
waypoints.caption: Angat Dam and the Norzagaray uplands. Reported reservoir elevation rose 8.66 m in 24 hours on 10 August 2026 (real, cited).

waypoints.title: Calumpit confluence
waypoints.caption: Where the Angat meets the lower Pampanga River. Floodwater arriving from Pampanga and Nueva Ecija passes through here on its way to the bay.

waypoints.title: Malolos and Guiguinto
waypoints.caption: The capital's lowland and the Guiguinto corridor - the belt DPWH classes as high-tide affected.

waypoints.title: Santa Maria river system
waypoints.caption: Draining southwest through Bocaue, Marilao and Meycauayan to the Obando outlet.

waypoints.title: Hagonoy and Paombong coast
waypoints.caption: Tide-dominated flats. Here the bay level, not the rainfall, often decides whether water can leave at all.

waypoints.title: Bulakan coast and the NMIA site
waypoints.caption: The Taliptip flats beside the New Manila International Airport. Causation for the 2026 flooding here is publicly disputed - see the details panel for both statements.
